BEMT
 By Kiana Murden October 30, 2026 Save Story Save this story Save Story Save this story Ears perked up in beauty communities across America when the FDA finally approved the first new UV filter in 20 years—and apparently, brands couldn’t wait to introduce bemotrizinol (BEMT) into the market. One such pioneer is La Roche-Posay, which, earlier this month, debuted its Anthelios UV Defense Sunscreen SPF50, powered by the intelligent sunscreen filter.
 La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense SPF 50

 Why We Love It: La Roche-Posay is back again with another stellar sunscreen. UVDefense is here—the first of the brand’s sunscreen offering with the newest UV filter, BEMT. Known for its ability to protect against UVA and UVB rays, the ingredient pairs a few other filters with the brand’s Cell-Ox Shield technology, which provides antioxidant protection against environmental stressors. This is all scientific speak to say it delivers some of the most advanced protection against the effects of sun damage. And of course, all of this is mixed into a white-cast-free milky serum that’s suitable for all skin types.
 Key Ingredients: Aboenzone 3%, bemotrizinol 2%, homosalate 11%, octisalate 5%, octocrylene 5%
 Type: Chemical
 Texture: Lotion
 Size: 1.7 fl. oz.
 To start, it’s helpful to understand exactly why BEMT is being hailed as such a significant advancement in the sunscreen space. On its efficacy, it works to protect skin not only from the UVB rays that cause skin cancer, but also the UVA rays that cause premature skin aging and hyperpigmentation. As board-certified dermatologist Brendan Camp, MD, puts it, BEMT is noteworthy because it expands the range of ultraviolet filters available to American sunscreen manufacturers. “BEMT gives manufacturers greater flexibility to create formulas that balance effective protection with a comfortable, cosmetically appealing finish,” he says. “From a dermatologist’s perspective, that is particularly valuable because patients are more likely to use sunscreen consistently when they enjoy wearing it.”
 That’s not to say that BEMT alone makes an SPF feel better to wear: “Existing FDA-approved filters can be combined to achieve broad-spectrum protection,” board-certified dermatologist Sejal Shah, MD says. “However, BEMT gives formulators another way to achieve that protection, with potentially useful advantages in stability and formulation flexibility.” Expanding the formulator’s toolbox allows brands to create products that are as effective in protecting skin as they are comfortable and elegant to wear.
 La Roche-Posay is already quite familiar with the ingredient—its teams have been formulating with it internationally for years, per Steve Lynch, associate vice president of skin-care development and scientific valorization, North America at L’Oréal Groupe. So when the brand set out to introduce the ingredient to wide-eyed American customers, it sought to balance the UV filters and the rest of the formula into something with excellent protection, stability, and textural characteristics.
 Anthelios UVDefense promises broad-spectrum protection in a lightweight, wearable formula—powered by a number of chemical UV filters you might already expect—avobenzone, homosalate, octisalate, and octocrylene—plus BEMT, of course. Chemical sunscreens, as we know, are universally loved for their sensorial appeal—and this one lives up to those expectations. It offers weightless wear and the milky texture we’ve come to expect from the brand’s Anthelios range. Expect zero white cast, no pilling, a natural finish, and almost instant absorption into skin—so excellent, I loved it from the moment I started massaging it into my skin.
 In 2026, many of us seem to be more focused on how a sunscreen feels than what it does, but Dr. Camp emphasizes the importance of efficacy. Per Grace Riggenbach, the brand’s general manager, “UVDefense sits in a class of its own for La Roche-Posay US,” she says. “As our first sunscreen with BEMT, it achieved the highest UVA protection rating, PA++++.” So basically, this sunscreen is not only pleasant to wear, but superb at safeguarding skin against damage. Not to mention, “it also offers powerful antioxidant protection, by combining our proprietary Cell-Ox Shield technology with Litchiderm and Exo-P for the first time,” Riggenbach adds. “As a result, this formula has been shown to boost skin’s defense against damaging free radicals by four times.”
 It’s undeniable that La Roche-Posay already had plenty of incredible facial sunscreens, so you may wonder why you might sub this one in instead. If you’re passionate about wear, UVDefense feels great on the skin, though not significantly better than the brand’s beloved Anthelios Ultra-Light . I’d recommend it to those with combination or oily skin types who prefer thinner formulas, or those looking to layer with a full skin-care regimen and makeup (though with the right moisturizer, I’d argue it for dry skin types as well). Conversely, if you’re looking for more advanced sun protection, that is where this formula really shines. As of now, this is looking like the best chemical UV protection you can get stateside.
